summary: DirtDoc is a solution that helps farmers monitor and cultivate crops that improve their soil's health. Using indigenous farming techniques, present data collection, and futuristic SI reasoning, our tool takes a look at your farm and determines the soil health of different parts of your land.  Then, it provides a bunch of options for what you can plant in each sector of the land to based on the climate and environmental synergies to help rejuvenate the soil, using indigenous farming techniques such as agroforestry and synergies like the three sisters. Our solution allows for the farmers to explore crop rotation strategies and adapt to changing conditions using libraries of indigenous crop strategies to help support future planning.
details: DirtDoc is a farmer's planning tool. It uses NASA API data to make judgments and provide strategies to help plan plots of land to prioritize soil health, maximize land longevity utilizing indigenous farming techniques lost to time. First, you select and draw a boundary to optimize. Next DirtDoc will collect and display general data over the entire area, allowing users to highlight specific sectors of their land. Each sector will have it's own suggestions for crops, forestry, and possible plant synergies, etc. Each sector will also have it's own timeline for future crop rotations. The benefit of uDirt is it's focus on healthy farming practices that help renew soil while increasing crop health. Combining past farming techniques, present NASA API data collection, and SI prediction and reasoning, we are able to focus on making the future sustainable, productive, and profitable. The intended impact is to help farmer's easily plan the land and have strategies that they can trust will keep the soil healthy and yields plenty. We used React, Vite, and Bootstrap to create the site. The maps are created by Leaflet. API's are handled through a python backend, powered by Render and Vercel for deployment. The SI reasoning is powered by Gemini. Our project is creative because we incorporate indigenous farming techniques like the three sisters and other healthy soil practices like agroforestry to support our reasoning for specific crop suggestions and cycles. A major factor in our decision making was the limits to NASA API geographical resolutions. Specifically NASA Powers only being able to use 15km by 15km resolution. To handle this, we used various APIs such as Landsat which have much more data and much smaller resolutions, allowing for more accurate judgement.
